goal: A pull request that changes real files cannot merge without a change record, so the brief, the evidence and the release note stop depending on the agent remembering.
changed: debrief.py check --base REF fails a pull request that changes a file outside the bookkeeping files and adds no record, and checks the records it added or edited.
--observe prints what would have failed and exits 0.
agent-kit's CI runs the check on every pull request, in observe mode. It does not block a merge yet.
debrief.py carries the same bookkeeping list as receipt.py and check-product.py, and a test holds the three equal.

claims.claim: The check fails a pull request with a source change and no record, passes one with a good record or with bookkeeping changes only, ignores commits that landed on the base since the branch, and exits 0 under --observe.
claims.check: tests/test_debrief.py (34 tests, throwaway git repos) under /usr/bin/python3 3.9.6 on macOS; make test (1,000 tests) under Python 3.12

claims.claim: On real history the check fails pull requests that had no record and passes the one that had.
claims.check: Replay over the last 30 merged agent-kit pull requests in a temporary checkout: 22 fail, 8 pass, no usage errors. #70 (55baad5) fails by name; #73 (7951786) passes.
claims.remaining: Whether all 22 deserved a record. Several were docs-only pull requests to files outside the bookkeeping list (REVIEW.md, docs/), and the replay cannot say if a record there is useful or noise.

claims.claim: The step runs in GitHub Actions on a pull request and reports without blocking.
claims.remaining: This pull request's own CI run is the first run of the step. Read its log once it finishes.

next.item: Drop --observe in agent-kit's CI after a week of pull requests
next.source: REVIEW.md, the rule that a new gate ships in observe mode
next.why_now: Not yet. The week shows whether docs-only pull requests make the check noisy, which decides whether the exempt list needs to grow first.
next.impact: Until then a pull request with no record still merges, and you only see it in the CI log.

next.item: Add the check to quality, agent-ledger and finances
next.why_now: Other projects were the main ask, and each already checks out a pinned agent-kit in CI, so it is one step per repo plus a pin bump.
next.impact: Those repos get a record, and so a release note, for every pull request that changes real files: about 16 of 24, 22 of 25 and 20 of 21 of their recent ones.

next.item: Have scaffold-product add the CI step to new and adopted repos
next.why_now: After the week of observe, so new repos start with a rule that is known to be quiet.
next.impact: A new project gets the brief, evidence and release notes with no setup.
